:::{#cor-cross-entropy-entropy}
#### Entropy is the cross-entropy of a distribution with itself

Let $X$ be a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) with [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) $p$.
Then

$$\crossentropyf{p}{p} = \entropyf{X}.$$

:::

::: proof

By the definition of [cross-entropy](#def-cross-entropy) with $q = p$, $\crossentropyf{p}{p} = \E{-\log p(X)}$.
The [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $-\log p(X)$ is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) $\Surprisalf{X}$ when $X$ is [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv),
and its [continuous](#def-surprisal-continuous) form $\surprisalf{X}$ when $X$ is continuous.
So $\crossentropyf{p}{p}$ is the [expectation](#def-expectation) of that surprisal, which is $\entropyf{X}$ by the definition of [entropy](#def-entropy).

:::
